data.description:
`bridge status` becomes the canonical way to check the bridge, and the heartbeat canary consumes it
on a schedule and escalates via tickets rather than being a parallel alarm.

Investigation found THREE existing indicators, none of them `.bridge-status.json`:
the heartbeat canary (the real production channel — hourly, files bug tickets tagged
`heartbeat-alert`/`binding-drift-alert`); `bridge_state/health/<pass_id>.json` (a complete per-pass
record, written on success AND failure with `failure_kind`, and read by NOBODY); and the tickets
branch itself (6,026 `chore: sync events from rebar reconciler [run <id>]` commits).

**The trap that must not be walked into:** there are TWO `bridge_state` directories.
`bridge_state/` (no dot) is GITIGNORED and never uploaded as an artifact — in production it is
written on an ephemeral runner and destroyed with it. `.tickets-tracker/.bridge_state/` is
committed. A status verb reading `health/` or `bridge_alerts/` would work perfectly for whoever
builds it and report NOTHING REAL in CI. On a dev checkout those files are five weeks stale while
the bridge ran through Aug 4.

**And the commit-back step has no `if:` condition** (`reconcile-bridge.yml:272`), so GHA skips it
whenever the reconciler step fails. A committed-only record would durably capture every success and
silently drop every hard failure — inverted.

Design: a ref-blob `refs/reconciler/last-pass` carries the minimal always-pushed truth (written by
the reconciler process itself, not the workflow), and a committed file carries rich detail. Crashed
vs running is answered by `refs/reconciler/lock`'s FENCE (a progress witness observed across one
lease) — never by comparing `heartbeat_ns` to the local clock, which reintroduces the clock-skew bug
the lease design eliminated.

Cross-environment safety: stamp the writer env and have status report only matching records, with a
distinct FOREIGN verdict rather than silently falling back. Do NOT use `.env-id` — it is gitignored
and regenerated per run, so an ephemeral runner gets a new one every pass. Use the configured
`REBAR_ENV_ID`. Only mutating passes write the durable record.

Consolidate on the way in: `health.record_pass` and `pass_io._write_pass_record` are already TWO
producers of this same fact, and the latter's docstring says it should commit to the tickets branch.
Do not create a third. Drop the dead `pre_fsck`/`post_fsck` fields and `capture_baseline`.

Salvage note corrected: `count_unresolved_alerts()` is NOT salvageable — zero `BRIDGE_ALERT` files
exist across all 39,160 files on `origin/tickets`, so it is provably always 0.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `bridge status` reports last run, in-flight state, and what needs attention, reading only DURABLE state
- [ ] A local run never reports a developer's own pass as production's
- [ ] Crashed is distinguished from running via the lock's fence across one lease, not a clock comparison
- [ ] A hard failure is still recorded despite the skipped commit-back step
- [ ] `--max-age` exits non-zero on staleness; `status` exits 0 while merely paused
- [ ] The canary calls `status` and stops querying the GitHub Actions API for the heartbeat
- [ ] Exactly one producer of the pass record remains
data.title: Build bridge status on durable state and have the canary consume it
